candidates.name: Royal Palace
candidates.content: The Royal Palace is one of the three official palaces of the Netherlands. It is at the disposal of King Willem-Alexander by the Act of Parliament. It was built in 1651 as the city hall of Amsterdam, in a period known as the Dutch

candidates.name: Nieuwe Kerk
candidates.price: By credit/debit card only: adult €19.50, student/youth €9.50, child under 12 free, free with Museumkaart
candidates.content: Used for royal coronations, including the crowning of King Willem-Alexander in 2013, and royal weddings, including his wedding to princess Máxima in 2002. The church is no longer used for services but is now a popular exhibition s

candidates.name: Allard Pierson Museum
candidates.content: The Allard Pierson Museum is the archaeological museum of the University of Amsterdam. The ancient civilizations of Egypt, Cyprus, the Greek world, Etruria and the Roman Empire are revived in this museum. Art objects and utensils,

candidates.name: Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder
candidates.content: One of the oldest museums in Amsterdam, this is a Catholic church stuffed into the upper stories of a house built in 1663, when Catholics were persecuted and had to disguise their churches. It's amazing to see how they fit worship

candidates.name: Oranje Voetbal Museum
candidates.content: The legacy of Dutch football started in the 1970s, when Total Football, a revolutionary Dutch style of football, shook the world. The Netherlands is the best football nation that never won the World Cup: it lost the final three ti

candidates.name: Rembrandt House
candidates.content: This is where the artist Rembrandt Harmensz van Rijn and his wife, Saskia, lived between 1639 and 1658. The house is a reconstruction of the painter’s life at that time and provides interesting insight. You will be able to see 260

candidates.name: Anne Frank House
candidates.hours: 9:00 - 22:00 (shorter on some national holidays, closed 25 September)
candidates.content: The house where the Jewish girl Anne Frank wrote her diary while hiding with her family from the Nazis. One must buy tickets online, only 20% are issued on the same day so buy them in advance. During high season tickets can be sol

candidates.name: Museum Het Grachtenhuis
candidates.content: Het Grachtenhuis is the gateway to the world-famous Canal District. Het Grachtenhuis tells the fascinating story of how Amsterdam's Canal District was created by a multi-media exhibition.

candidates.name: Cat Cabinet
candidates.content: A cat museum. Housed in a beautiful restored palatial home in an upscale area street - very Masterpiece Theater. It was opened by the homeowner after his favourite cat died... and he still lives in the home. Lots of cat-related ar

candidates.name: Museum Willet-Holthuysen
candidates.content: It is the only fully furnished canalside patrician house in Amsterdam that is open to the public. The museum has a large collection of silverware, plates, and books from the Dutch Golden Age. It also has a substantial collection o

candidates.name: Westerkerk
candidates.content: Built in 1620-1631, located on Westermarkt near the Anne Frank House. You can climb the tower (with a guide only) every half hour, M-Sa €6. The tower is also open in the winter by group appointment (maximum 10 people) for €70/hr.

candidates.name: Wereldmuseum Amsterdam
candidates.content: Ethnographic and cultural museum about Africa, Asia and South America. Includes an excellent cafe which sells food from around the world. Tickets are discounted if reserved online.

candidates.name: Natura Artis Magistra Zoo
candidates.price: Youth (3 to 9 years) €18, adult (10 to 64 years) €21.50, seniors (65 +) €17.50
candidates.content: An entry ticket for Artis also provides admission to the Planetarium, the Aquarium and the Zoological Museum. Artis is also a botanical garden, with plants and trees gathered from all over the world, just like the animal species.

candidates.name: H'ART
candidates.price: Standard (adults and children aged 18 or over) €22.50, children up to 17 years old free
candidates.content: Founded as an outpost of the Hermitage in St Petersburg, ties were severed with the parent institution following Russia's war in Ukraine. After a hasty rebrand, the H'ART museum reopened in April 2022 with a focus on Dutch heritag

candidates.name: Scheepvaartmuseum
candidates.content: Het Scheepvaartmuseum reopened in late 2011 following major renovations. Stimulating, interactive exhibitions allow visitors to explore 500 years of maritime history. The building, called the Arsenal, is impressive. The Central Sq

candidates.name: Verzetsmuseum
candidates.content: Museum showing what Amsterdam and Holland were like during Nazi occupation. Has a very nice children's section. If you are visiting with kids and want to go to a museum about the Second World War in the Netherlands this is definit

candidates.name: Rijksmuseum
candidates.price: adults, European Youth Card, children free, no student discounts
candidates.content: The largest and most prestigious museum for art and history in the Netherlands: works by Vermeer, Rembrandt, and other Dutch masters. Its garden has a curious collection of architecture and has free entrance during museum opening

candidates.name: Stedelijk Museum
candidates.content: The Stedelijk Museum is the municipal museum of modern art. It has a long history, as it first opened in 1874 and has been at its current location since 1895. It was reopened in 2012 after a renovation that took four years: the ne

candidates.name: Van Gogh Museum
candidates.content: This museum is dedicated to Vincent van Gogh, a late 19th-century Post-Impressionist Dutch painter. Tickets are available online only, and can be booked out weeks in advance during busy periods. In the museum are many, but not all

candidates.name: Amsterdam Centraal railway station
candidates.content: This beautiful building is an attraction in itself, so if you did not arrive in Amsterdam by train, it is well worth making a special trip to look at the station's facade. The station was built between 1881 and 1889 on three artif

candidates.name: Begijnhof
candidates.content: The Begijnhof is a late medieval enclosed courtyard with the houses of beguines (Roman Catholic women living in a semi-religious community). It is a very picturesque group of historic buildings, mostly private dwellings. House num

candidates.name: Esnoga
candidates.content: The most prominent synagogue of the city centre, the Esnoga dates back from 1675 and is built in an austere Classicist style. In 1492, Spain expelled its Jewish population as part of the Inquisition, and many fled to Portugal. One

candidates.name: Oude Kerk
candidates.content: The oldest of the five main churches in the historic centre, and probably the oldest building in Amsterdam. It is right in the heart of the Red Light District. You can climb the tower from April to September on Saturday and Sunday

candidates.name: Zuiderkerk
candidates.content: Built in 1603-1611. Located on Zuiderkerkhof ("Southern Graveyard"). Now an information centre on housing and planning. You can visit the tower from April to September Monday to Saturday (with guide only) every half-hour, cost €6.

candidates.name: Amsterdam Museum
candidates.content: A museum about the history of Amsterdam.

candidates.name: Jewish Historical Museum
candidates.content: Jewish Historical Museum. History of the Jewish people, culture and religion.

candidates.name: Amsterdam Pipe Museum
candidates.content: Unique collection of smoking pipes in an authentic canal house from 1670. In the historic ambience of the collector's house, his collection of pipes covering 2,500 years is displayed. Visitors get a personal tour by enthusiast vol

candidates.name: Museum Van Loon
candidates.content: 17th century house with interior restored with furnishings to how it looked in the 18th century. Also interesting to see a garden you would not normally see from the streets.

candidates.name: KunstRAI
candidates.content: A modern art fair in the RAI exhibition and conference centre. If you want to know what the latest developments are in Dutch galleries, this is where to find them all in one place.

candidates.name: Museumnacht
candidates.content: Long before the film came out, this "night at the museum" attracts new crowds at the traditional Amsterdam museums with special performances at unusual locations. Do as the locals do and hire a bike to go from one place to the oth

candidates.name: Imagine Film Festival
candidates.content: A two weeks celebration of drive-in, exploitation and cult films, generally of the lower budget variety. Takes up all the screening rooms of the EYE Film Institute in Noord.

candidates.name: Hash, Marihuana and Hemp Museum
candidates.content: Opened for over twenty years, the Hash Museum is dedicated to debunking the lies and demonization about one of our most useful plants, the hemp plant. Although small, busy and seriously overpriced, it is a well-done museum where p

candidates.name: Madame Tussauds
candidates.content: The well-known franchise of wax museums also has a branch in Amsterdam. It's a major tourist attraction so expect a steep entry fee and long queues. Unique to this branch are waxworks of famous Dutch people including Willem-Alexan

candidates.name: Torture Museum
candidates.content: You'd think one museum about torture would be enough, but no, not in Amsterdam. However, this was the first torture museum in the city centre, and is at least somewhat more authentic than the copycat. The museum depicts the histor

candidates.name: Pathé Tuschinski
candidates.content: Since its opening in 1921, Tuschinski has been the country's most breathtaking film theatre. It's worth a visit if only for its interior, a spectacular mix of Art Nouveau, Amsterdam School and Art Deco styles. If possible, get a t

candidates.name: Electrische Museumtramlijn Amsterdam
candidates.price: Adult fares vary from €3.50 to €12.50 with reduced rates for seniors (65+) and children (4-11)
candidates.hours: Sundays, April-November, plus Easter & Pentecost Mon, 11:00-17:00
candidates.content: On operating days, the museum runs various vintage trams on two routes. Line 30 runs every 30 minutes along on a 7-km museum rail line to Amstelveen with stops along the route. Station Amstelveen is perhaps the most interesting st

candidates.name: Holland Festival
candidates.content: A performing arts festival that brings together events from all over the world in the fields of music, opera, theater and dance.

candidates.name: Julidans
candidates.content: International contemporary dance festival, always showing the latest developments in modern dance.

candidates.name: Sail Amsterdam
candidates.content: Tall-ships from all over the world come to visit the Amsterdam harbour every five years, the next one is planned in 2030.

candidates.name: International Documentary Film Festival (IDFA)
candidates.content: The largest festival in the world for documentary films with screenings of about 200 documentary films and videos.

candidates.name: Amsterdam Light Festival
candidates.content: Outdoor light installations/artworks exposition in the canals of Binnenstad. Each year the festival has a different theme.

candidates.name: Amsterdam Dungeon
candidates.content: The Amsterdam Dungeon is a horror tour through several dark chambers with live actors.

candidates.name: Boom Chicago
candidates.content: The Amsterdam comedy institution since 1993. English language sketch and improv comedy show with extensive use of video, music and the internet. The troupe is sharp and skewers current events, trends and life and local events in A

candidates.name: EYE Film Institute Netherlands
candidates.content: EYE is an institute dedicated to the preservation of film for future generations. It is the successor of the Filmmuseum. It has four film theatres with alternative screenings such as art films. In April the Imagine Film Festival i

candidates.name: Carré Theatre
candidates.content: When the theatre was founded in 1887, it was meant as a permanent circus building. It is mainly used for musicals, cabaret performances and pop concerts.

candidates.name: Concertgebouw
candidates.content: Famous for its orchestra and its acoustics (among the top ten in the world), this is one of the world's most frequently visited concert halls. Classical music is the main fare, but they also bring other kinds of music on stage. Th

candidates.name: Boats4rent Boat Rental
candidates.hours: open every day from March to October
candidates.content: Boats4rent is a boat rental where you can rent a boat without a skipper. With a three or four hour rental you can make a private trip on the Amsterdam canals and the Amstel river.

candidates.name: Amsterdam Dance Event
candidates.content: Usually held during the second last weekend in October, this electronic music annual festival gathers cream of the crop faces from the house and techno scenes. Buy your tickets in advance to avoid paying more at the door and havin

candidates.name: Sugar Factory
candidates.content: Bit of a remarkable place that integrates art, music, culture, theatre and nightclub into one. It has a relaxed atmosphere with an eccentric, artistic audience.

candidates.name: TonTon Club West
candidates.content: TonTon Club is an excellent place for a good night out. The place has a unique atmosphere with Japan as its inspiration. Upstairs there are arcades and button bashers, downstairs there's room for drinks and board games. You can al

candidates.name: Filter
candidates.content: Small eco-friendly coffeebar situated in the lobby of hotel Ecomama. Serves great coffee, breakfast and a small selection of sweet and savoury treats. Also organic tea, juice and the best grilled-cheese sandwiches. Have a relaxed

candidates.name: Hannekes Boom
candidates.content: One of Amsterdam's hidden secrets, Hannekes Boom is a cosy, somewhat ramshackle, bar with a waterfront along the IJ. It's a great place to just hang out and have a beer. Not for clubbers, but for those looking for a relaxing under

candidates.name: Brouwerij de Prael
candidates.price: Brewery tour or , beer tasting with four beers €10
candidates.hours: Beer shop 12:00-19:00, tasting room Tue-Sat 12:00-24:00, Sun 12:00-23:00
candidates.content: A brewery, tasting room and beer shop all in one.

candidates.name: Cracked Kettle
candidates.content: This beer, wine, and spirits shop carries independent, unique, and rare bottles. The staff are friendly, but the space is quite confined and obtaining bottles from the very top shelves requires assistance and a dust rag.

candidates.name: In De Wildeman
candidates.content: A very well stocked beer café, or actually beer tasting room (bierproeflokaal) in the centre of the inner city. 17 beers (usually from various countries) and a cider on draught, and about 250 different bottled beers offered. There

candidates.name: Wynand Fockink
candidates.content: Wynand Fockink is a distillery that started in 1679. They offer distillery tours, but you must reserve at least a week in advance as they fill up quickly. It is also a tasting room and a liquor store. They have numerous liquors, b

candidates.name: Belgique
candidates.content: One of the smallest bars in Amsterdam, there is seating for at most 15 people. Specialising in Belgian beers, extensive menu that includes some hard to find beers on tap. This place is smoke friendly so don't be surprised to see p

candidates.name: Cuba
candidates.content: Great bar, really nice atmosphere, close to the Red Light District with a nice terrace in the summer. Selection of cheap cocktails and long island ice tea.

candidates.name: Molly Malones Irish Pub
candidates.content: Authentic Irish pub with food. Mix of expatriates, locals and tourists, friendly staff, on a canal off the Zeedijk, close to Centraal Station and Warmoesstraat. Open every night, live music in the week-ends and large-screen televi

candidates.name: Schuim
candidates.content: The super comfy cafe is a great place to spend entire rainy days at a time. It heats up quite a bit at night. Pot smoking seems to be tolerated even though Schuim is definitely not a "coffeeshop".

candidates.name: Speijk
candidates.content: Awesome bar with lost of fun, artsy crazy locals. Various DJ play different styles. Open till late in the morning. Best place to meet laid-back and awesome Amsterdammers!!

candidates.name: Irish Pub Slainte
candidates.content: An Irish pub that also serves very inexpensive food like cheese sandwiches. Everything you can expect from an Irish pub nearby the Oude Kerk and nearby the Red Light District.

candidates.name: Gebr. Niemeijer
candidates.content: French-style bakery with pastries, croissants, breads, sandwiches all baked fresh on premises. Open for breakfast and lunch, eat-in or takeaway. Bring the kids and eat in the small playroom upstairs.

candidates.name: OCHA
candidates.content: This used to be just the little "Thai snackbar around the corner", but since a raving review in the local newspaper Het Parool, big crowds are waiting in line to get seated during dinnertime. The scenery is simple and the restaura

candidates.name: Thaise Snackbar Bird
candidates.content: Very crowded little snack bar with Thai food. Not to be confused with the restaurant of the same owner, on the other side of the street. Try the chicken in oyster sauce.

candidates.name: De Blauwe Hollander
candidates.content: Dutch restaurant with an extensive menu of hearty home-cooked dishes like herrings, pea soup and hutspot. Unlike most restaurants in this area, this one gets local diners too, and if it gets crowded enough you may have to share ta

candidates.name: Biertuin
candidates.content: Oktoberfest-style biergarten, so expect long tables and a wide variety of bottled beers available. It has a nice atmosphere during warm summer evenings. Try the Hamburger Deluxe or chicken menus. And come early, as it is often cro

candidates.name: Cafe Kadijk
candidates.content: Cafe Kadijk is a small Indonesian restaurant that offers good food at a decent price. The restaurant has a coffee shop vibe and is located in a "trendy" area. Just outside Amsterdam's city centre, it is a bit of a walk away from t

candidates.name: Dosa
candidates.content: They specialise in traditional Southern Indian cuisine, especially the eponymous 'Dosa' (a rice and lentil pancake with a variety of fillings). The food is outstanding and well worth hunting out. The dosas are exceptional and a tr

candidates.name: Albina
candidates.content: It's cheap and very good. If you arrive around dinnertime you probably have to wait for a table. The surroundings are depressing but the food is so good you will come back anyway.

candidates.name: Marmaris Grill & Pizza
candidates.content: Relatively up-market Turkish/Mediterranean restaurant in the fancy new building opposite station Bijlmer-Arena. Great food, presentation and service - definitely worth the price. On cold days, avoid sitting anywhere near the door

candidates.name: Oma Ietje
candidates.content: Inevitably, hipsters have even found their way into the Bijlmer. Part-funded by crowdfunding. Very worthy 'Swedish style' coffee house. Coffee, biological lemonade and cakes. Also showcases art by local artists.

candidates.name: Van der Linde
candidates.content: Its officially a bakery, but they don't sell bread. They do sell Amsterdam's most famous whipped ice cream, lovely almond cookies and cakes. The texture is really creamy and soft, it melts easily and they put it in a cone with a s

candidates.name: Pasta Pasta
candidates.content: Serves delicious pastas, made just as you want them. Choose a sauce, topping and pasta for a tasty, but well-priced meal.

candidates.name: Bloemenmarkt
candidates.content: The world's only floating flower market, open daily on the Singel between Koningsplein and Muntplein. It is very touristy, but you could do worse than buying your tulips here. Make sure you buy pre-approved bulbs if taking them to

candidates.name: Noordermarkt
candidates.content: On Monday morning the Noordermarkt is a flea market selling fabrics, records, second-hand clothing etc., and forms part of the Lapjesmarkt mentioned above. On Saturday, the Noordermarkt is a biological food market, selling a wide

candidates.name: Waterloopleinmarkt
candidates.content: A well-known but fairly overrated market near the city hall. Partly flea market, partly alternative and second hand clothing and accessories. More oriented towards tourists than to locals.

candidates.name: Albert Cuyp Market
candidates.content: Largest street market in Amsterdam, and the best-known street market in the country. It is iconic for the "De Pijp" neighborhood and its working-class inhabitants. There is something for everyone here, whether you're looking for d

candidates.name: Spui
candidates.content: Every Friday and Sunday a market is held on the Spui. Friday has books on sale, while Sundays are all about art and antiques.

december.text: Amsterdam is a large city and a major tourist destination, so you can visit it all year round. However, in winter the days are short (8 hours of daylight around Christmas between 08:45 and 16:30), and the weather may be too cold to walk around the city comfortably, let alone cycle. January and February are the col

They are known as snorders and most easily reached by mobile phone. Rides within Zuidoost (the Bijlmer) range from to , whereas Zuidoost-Centre can run up to . Snorders have a sh

Ice skating is a longstanding tradition in the Netherlands, and you will sometimes see locals skating down the canals when they freeze over in the winter. However, the ice has to be thick enough for you to be able to do this safely, and this requires temperatures to stay below continuously for at least 2 weeks. Take th

The late-medieval city also had smaller chapels such as the Sint Olofskapel (circa 1440) on Zeedijk, and convent chapels such as the Agnietenkapel on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal 231 (originally 1470), now the University of Amsterdam museum. Later churches included the Oosterkerk (1669) in the eastern islands, and the hea

Amsterdam's culinary scene boasts a vibrant tapestry of flavours, offering a rich variety of dining experiences. The city unfolds as a treasure trove for those craving Asian cuisine, albeit catered to the milder local palate. Adventurous taste buds, fear not – it's not impossible to find spicy food.

Check out bitterballen, fried breaded ragout balls, and kroketten (the same, but shaped like a cylinder), but take care not to burn your mouth. Also don't forget to try a traditional herring or a broodje haring (herring sandwich), available from fish stalls around the city. Herring in Amsterdam is usually served with o
Chinese New Year: Celebrated with festivities in Chinatown.

Museumplein: Amsterdam celebrates the holy day of Sint Nicholaas on 5 December as Christmas in the Dam Square also known as "Christmas Square". However, on Christmas Day, i.e. 25 December, the people of Amsterdam are also getting used to celebrating Christmas alongside English speakers.

ICE* Amsterdam: During winter time there is an amazing ice rink in Amsterdam at the Museumplein. The open-air ice skating rink that covers 1400 m2 can be found at its usual spot in the heart of Amsterdam and is open daily for all visitors.
